wire_article.text: City officials said on Monday that the regional transit authority will extend late-night bus service on four routes starting next month, after a six-month pilot showed ridership between 11 p.m. and 2 a.m. rose by about 18 percent. The authority's board approved the change in a 7-2 vote. Board chair Maria Lopez said the extension would cost roughly $2.4 million a year and would be funded through a mix of state grants and fare revenue. Two board members who voted against the plan said they were concerned about the long-term budget, noting that the state grant expires in 2028. The authority said it would publish quarterly ridership figures and review the program after one year. Riders at a public hearing last week largely supported the change, with several shift workers saying the pilot had cut their commute times. The new schedule takes effect on the first Sunday of next month.
